title: The nimshal: Yachid, Echad, Kadmon in the Essence, and a fourth level after the tzimtzum
overview: Chapter 11 is the *nimshal* of chapter 10, "almost a repetition of it": the three levels traced in the soul are now traced in the Essence of the *Or Ein Sof* before the *tzimtzum*. In *Yachid* the ten *sefiros* are hidden in the Essence itself, every attribute infinite, down to kingship and *Ana Emloch*. The whole *hishtalshelus* arose only because He is kind, and to Him it is one little *prat*, like scratching your ear while you talk; only the study of *Chassidus* reminds Him what He wanted it for. In *Echad* the powers seem to come out and stay one. In *Kadmon* the exact *shiur* is ready down to the end of *Asiya*, made the way a cat jumps: by looking at the mouse, not at the jump. Then a fourth level: the *reshimu* and the *Kav*, contracted and still a level of the Essence. Here the sandwich shows what *hafshatas hagashmiyus* really means: the physical act comes from the *Aibershter*, not from the will. The chapter ends by reading the levels into "Blessed is He who spoke".

sections.title: Yachid: the ten sefiros hidden in the concealment of the Essence itself
sections.summary: Chapter 11 is the *nimshal* of chapter 10: the three levels shown in the soul are now traced above, in the Essence of the *Or Ein Sof* before the *tzimtzum*, starting with *Yachid*, where the ten *sefiros* are hidden in the Essence itself. This is not what the Rebbe Rashab's *Ayin Beis* is about.

phrases.he: (יא) והנמשל מכל הנזכר לעיל בנפש
phrases.en: (11) And the *nimshal* (what the analogy stands for) of all that was said above about the soul

phrases.he: יובן למשכיל
phrases.en: will be understood by the thoughtful

phrases.he: למעלה בעצמות אור אין סוף שלפני הצמצום
phrases.en: above, in the Essence of the *Or Ein Sof* (the infinite light) before the *tzimtzum* (contraction),

phrases.he: שנקרא יחיד
phrases.en: which is called *Yachid* (singular).

phrases.he: וכלול גם שם מעשר ספירות,
phrases.en: So over there it also includes in it ten *sefiros*,

phrases.he: ונקרא עשר ספירות הגנוזות בהעלם העצמות ממש
phrases.en: and they are called the ten *sefiros* hidden in the concealment of the Essence itself.

blocks.text: Chapter 11 is basically the continuation of chapter 10: it is the *nimshal*. Chapter 10 laid out, in the soul, that there is and there isn't, and that there are three levels: the *etzem* (essence) of the light itself; then how it is ready for *hispashtus* (spreading forth); and then how it is ready for *hispashtus* in the actual *prat* (particular) on the outside. Now the same is said above, in the Essence of the *Or Ein Sof* before the *tzimtzum*, which is called *Yachid*: **So over there it also includes in it ten**.

Notice that he gives a whole long definition. It is not just "the ten hidden *sefiros*", because the ten *sefiros* in *Adam Kadmon* are also called the ten hidden *sefiros*. These are the ten *sefiros* hidden **in the concealment of the Essence itself**.

blocks.question: From the way the Rebbe Rashab describes it, the ten hidden sefiros seem to be in Kadmon. Is he talking about the same thing?
blocks.text: The Rashab is not talking about *Yachid*. He is not even talking about *Kadmon*, because *Kadmon* is not an actual *hispashtus*; it is only a possible *hispashtus*. The Rashab is talking about the *hispashtus* of the *Or Ein Sof*. Here the Mitteler Rebbe says that these three levels are in the *Atzmus Or Ein Sof* (the Essence of the infinite light), including *Kadmon*. What the Rashab is talking about comes after the *kli* (vessel) of *Kadmon*. If you want to put a name on it, it is not even *Malchus* of *Kadmon*; it is *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Kadmon*. What he is talking about in *Ayin Beis* (the Rashab's series of discourses) is the *hispashtus* of the *Or Ein Sof*.

This is basically what Reb Hillel Paritcher said, which came up before: there are two levels in the light and two levels in the *Atzmus* (the Essence). In the *Atzmus* there is "He" and there is "He alone"; in the light there is the *etzem* of the *Or Ein Sof* and the *hispashtus* of the *Or Ein Sof*. This whole thing here, including *Kadmon*, is the *etzem* of the light. In the *etzem* of the *Or Ein Sof* it is ready; it is not spreading forth yet. It is only ready for spreading forth, estimated for it. What the Rebbe Rashab talks about over there is a whole different thing: what he has a hundred chapters on is here not even a dot. It is between the lines; it is not even one word here.

It comes after you figure out the whole thing: after it is ready to spread forth, by the end of *Kadmon*, where, as he said, it is *mamash* (actually) ready to spread forth but did not actually spread forth yet, because something holds it back. It is not actual. It is like the spreading of the life to give life to the body, which is ready to go out; it is not the spreading forth yet. Over there he is talking about something that here is not even a dot, and over there it is a hundred chapters. It is a very advanced book. It is very easy to confuse the two if you don't know what each is actually talking about.

"If that's a hundred chapters, imagine what chapter 10 is going to be." Chapter 10, by the Rebbe Rashab, would be a thousand chapters. And the whole of *Ayin Beis* does not even cover what comes towards the end of this book. It is almost all about the first few chapters, and not even all of what they talk about. "And it's a whole different approach." "I wouldn't call it a different approach; he's just talking about different details." "The approach to the *tzimtzum* is different; he's talking about a different matter with it, a different *tzimtzum*." "Right, it's a different matter within the *tzimtzum*."

blocks.title: The schools of Kabbala do not disagree
blocks.text: There is a *maamar* (discourse) of the Rebbe, "either in *yud-daled* or *yud-zayin*": it is not that the Rashab is disagreeing with the Mitteler Rebbe. That is why he tells you. A different approach would mean that you are disagreeing. And by the way, the real approaches in Kabbala do not disagree. The Ramak and the Arizal are not really disagreeing: they are talking about different things; it is a different view of the same thing. And the Rebbe Rashab does not even give a different view. He is explaining a different matter in the *seder hishtalshelus* (the chain of descending worlds), and he tells you so: this is not what the Mitteler Rebbe was talking about.

By the time the Rebbe Rashab would finish with it, these 78 pages would be like ten thousand chapters, at least. Here, especially in the later chapters, there are basically two chapters on *yichuda tata'a* (the lower unity), because most of the *yichuda tata'a* he discusses is still in *Malchus* of *Atzilus*. Then one chapter discusses the whole of *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya*, another one or two how it comes through the *galgalim* (celestial orbits) and the constellations, and the final chapter the *kelipos* (lit. husks). This book covers everything; that one does not. It is only partial, not the whole *seder hishtalshelus*. It does not give you the framework: when you look at it, you see that it assumes you already know the framework.

sections.title: The desire for kindness: why there is a world at all, and why to Him it is a fidget
sections.summary: The simple will for the whole *hishtalshelus* arose only because He is kind in Himself, and to Him the whole chain is one little particular, like scratching your ear while you talk; the study of *Chassidus* is the exception. Every particular kindness is already in the *hiyuli* desire for kindness, made of ten, without even unity.

phrases.he: כמו בחינת חפץ חסד
phrases.en: Like the *chafetz chesed* (desire for kindness)

phrases.he: שכלול בבחינת עצמיות דאור אין סוף,
phrases.en: that is included in the very Essence of the *Or Ein Sof*,

phrases.he: שמחמתו וסיבתו היה הרצון הפשוט לכל ההשתלשלות,
phrases.en: because of which, and caused by which, came the simple will for the whole *hishtalshelus* (chain of descent),

phrases.he: שזהו בדבר פרט
phrases.en: which is in a *davar prat* (a particular thing).

blocks.text: Because of this *chafetz chesed* in the very Essence came the original *ratzon hapashut* (simple will) for all of *hishtalshelus*. **which is in a** *davar prat*: as far as the *Aibershter* (the One Above) is concerned, this whole *hishtalshelus* is considered just one little *prat*. It is not the whole thing He is into; it is like one little *prat*.

blocks.title: Fidgeting with your ear
blocks.text:
In some place there is a *mashal* (analogy) that it is not just a *prat*; it is even less than a *prat*. Right now we are talking, and one of us scratches his neck, or fidgets his foot while we are talking. That is a *prat*, and it is coming from you: you did it. If you didn't fidget your foot, it wouldn't fidget. And yet it is almost as if you don't even know about it. It is not just insignificant: while you are all into this talking, you *mamash* almost don't even realize that you scratched your head a little.

Some people have a habit of playing with their ear. You tell them, "How come you always play with your ear?" "Oh, do I? Do I really?" "Yeah, you do." "Wait a minute, I didn't even realize I was doing it." "What do you mean you didn't realize you were doing it? If you didn't do it, it wouldn't get done. Your brain had to send the message to your hand through the nerves; otherwise how would you fidget with your ear?"

That is the whole thing that it says about Rosh Hashana: we have to bring back the *Malchus* (kingship), and, as it says, the remembrances: you have to remind the *Aibershter*. You have to remind Him that He is there. He is off into His thing, whatever His thing is.
"He's on the phone with his brother learning *Shaar HaYichud*."

sensitivity.reason: The joke pictures G-d as the speaker himself is in this class: on the phone with his brother, learning this book; it identifies the student as his brother.

blocks.text: In the meantime this world is like a *prat*. This whole thing is just like a *prat*.

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב בעץ חיים בהקדמה,
phrases.en: As is written in *Etz Chaim*, in the introduction:

phrases.he: כשעלה ברצונו הפשוט כו'
phrases.en: "When it arose in His simple will..."

phrases.he: ובודאי סיבת עליית הרצון הפשוט בעצמותו
phrases.en: And certainly the reason the simple will arose in His Essence

phrases.he: היינו רק כי חפץ חסד הוא בעצמו
phrases.en: is only that He is *chafetz chesed* in Himself.

phrases.he: על כן עלה ברצונו להטיב חסדו
phrases.en: Therefore it arose in His will to bestow His kindness,

phrases.he: להיות מקור למקור להשתלשלות דקו וחוט כו'
phrases.en: to be a source of the source for the *hishtalshelus* of the *Kav* and the thread.

blocks.text: The *Etz Chaim* says in its introduction, "When it arose in His simple will", and certainly the reason the simple will arose is only that He is kind in Himself. It is like a kind person. They say, "Why did you do a kind thing?" Because he's a kind person. **Therefore it arose in His will to bestow His kindness**: that is why He decided to do a good thing, to be a source of the source for what comes to be outside.

But that this whole world is just a *prat*, an insignificant *prat*, applies to the whole world. It does not apply to the study of *Chassidus* (Chassidic teaching). It is just the opposite. Here we are talking about the *etzem*, and that is really what He was into, the reason He doesn't even realize that He is just scratching His ear. The actual study of *Chassidus* is the *etzem* of the whole thing, and that is what reminds Him: "Oh, that's right, that's what I wanted the whole world for." And that is already from the *etzem*.

blocks.question: What does he mean by makor l'makor, a source of the source?
blocks.text: He is not actually a source for the world, and also not actually a *makor l'makor*. But you have to say something. Finally you have to say that He is the source. As the last chapter said, first of all you have to speak of the *Mekora d'Kula* (the Source of everything): even though He is not an actual source as far as He Himself goes, nonetheless that is where it came from. So you have to say a source, but you can't say a source, so we say a source of the source. "If you don't like to say a *makor*, so you'll have to say a *makor l'makor l'makor*," and then four times and five times. So we say it just two times, and you understand that it is really not even that.

phrases.he: והרי זה על דרך דוגמא
phrases.en: This is by way of example:

phrases.he: כשמחמת עצמיות המדה דחפץ חסד הכלולה בבחינת יחידה כנזכר לעיל,
phrases.en: when, because of the essence of the attribute of *chafetz chesed* that is included in the *yechida* (the essence of the soul), as said above,

phrases.he: עולה ברצונו לעשות טוב וחסד בדבר פרט כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: it rises in his will to do good and kindness in a particular thing, as said above,

phrases.he: שבא בגלוי מן העלמו ההיולי דחפץ חסד,
phrases.en: which comes into revelation from the *hiyuli* (raw potential) concealment of the *chafetz chesed*,

phrases.he: לכלול כל מה שיעלה בפרט ברצונו להטיב
phrases.en: to include all that will arise in particular in his will to do good:

phrases.he: הכל בא מחמתו וכחו כו'
phrases.en: everything comes because of it and its power.

blocks.text: By way of example: because of the essence of the *chafetz chesed* in the *yechida*, it rises in a man's will to do good in a particular thing, to give a person a sandwich. That particular comes out of the hidden *chafetz chesed*, and anything that he will ever have a will to do good in was already included in it. **everything comes because of it and its power**: the power of the *hiyuli* (raw potential) *chafetz chesed*.

phrases.he: וכמו שבגלוי רצון שבא מחמת חפץ חסד זה,
phrases.en: And just as the revealed will that comes because of this *chafetz chesed*

phrases.he: כלול מי', חב''ד ומדות כו'
phrases.en: is made of ten, *Chabad* (chachma, bina and daas) and *middos* (emotional attributes),

phrases.he: מזה מוכרח שגם בבחינת חפץ חסד ההיולי שכלול בעצמות ממש,
phrases.en: it follows that the *hiyuli* *chafetz chesed* included in the Essence itself

phrases.he: כלול מי', חכמה ומדות כו'
phrases.en: is also made of ten, *chachma* (wisdom) and *middos*;

phrases.he: רק שלא יתכן בהם לומר גם ענין ההתכללות והאחדות,
phrases.en: only that one cannot say of them even inclusion and unity,

phrases.he: אחר שכלול בעצמות בבחינת היולי עדיין כו'
phrases.en: since they are included in the Essence, still as *hiyuli*.

blocks.text: Just as the revealed will that comes from this *chafetz chesed* is made of ten, *Chabad* and *middos*, as the last chapter said, so the *hiyuli* *chafetz chesed* included in the Essence itself is made of ten, **only that one cannot say of them even inclusion and unity**, because they are still included in the Essence as *hiyuli*.

This whole chapter you can really learn very fast, because it is exactly the last chapter; it is almost a repetition of it. The last chapter was in the *mashal*, in a person. Now we are in the *nimshal*, but it is all the same: now it says exactly the same thing in the *nimshal*.

sections.title: Every attribute alike, down to kingship and Ana Emloch
sections.summary: *Gevura*, *netzach*, *tiferes* and every other attribute, down to the kingship of the *Ein Sof*, are infinite and made of ten in the Essence. Even *Ana Emloch*, the thought of kingship coming into a particular, is wholly included in *Yachid*.

phrases.he: וכמו כן במדה זולתה,
phrases.en: And so too with another attribute,

phrases.he: כמו מדת הגבורה או הנצח והתפארת וכהאי גוונא
phrases.en: such as the attribute of *gevura* (might), or *netzach* and *tiferes*, and the like:

phrases.he: הכל הוא כלול בעצמיות דאור אין סוף שנקרא טהירו עילאה
phrases.en: it is all included in the Essence of the *Or Ein Sof*, which is called *tehiru ila'a* (the upper purity),

phrases.he: והוא הנקרא יחיד שלמעלה מאחד פשוט כו'
phrases.en: and that is what is called *Yachid*, which is above simple One.

blocks.text: He reads straight on: so too with every other attribute, *gevura*, *netzach*, *tiferes* and the like. It is all included in the Essence of the *Or Ein Sof*, the *tehiru ila'a*, and that is *Yachid*, **which is above simple One**.

phrases.he: עד בחינת מדת המלוכה
phrases.en: Up to the attribute of kingship

phrases.he: בעצמות אור אין סוף
phrases.en: in the Essence of the *Or Ein Sof*,

phrases.he: שנקרא מלכות דאין סוף
phrases.en: which is called *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof*:

phrases.he: גם הוא כלול בבחינת היולי העצמי דעצמות אור אין סוף
phrases.en: it too is included in the essential *hiyuli* of the Essence of the *Or Ein Sof*,

phrases.he: שהוא בבחינת אין סוף ממש
phrases.en: which is truly infinite.

phrases.he: וכמו שחפץ חסד בבחינת אין סוף ממש בעצמות,
phrases.en: And just as *chafetz chesed* is truly infinite in the Essence,

phrases.he: או לחכמתו אין סוף,
phrases.en: or "His wisdom is infinite,"

phrases.he: כך מדת ההתנשאות
phrases.en: so the attribute of *hisnasus* (exaltation)

phrases.he: שכלול בעצמות אור אין סוף
phrases.en: that is included in the Essence of the *Or Ein Sof*

phrases.he: הוא בבחינת אין סוף
phrases.en: is infinite,

phrases.he: וכלול מי' בהעלם העצמות,
phrases.en: and it is made of ten in the concealment of the Essence:

phrases.he: שהוא בחינת הרצון והתענוג וחכמה ומדות שבמדות המלוכה
phrases.en: the will and the delight, and *chachma* and *middos*, that are in the attribute of kingship.

blocks.text: So it goes **Up to the attribute of kingship** in the Essence of the *Or Ein Sof*, called *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof*: here he is talking about *Malchus* of *Yachid*. It too is included in the essential *hiyuli*, and it is truly infinite. Just as *chafetz chesed* in the Essence is infinite, so the attribute of *hisnasus* is infinite, "and this is *mamash* exactly what it said in the last chapter." It too is made of ten: the will and the delight, *chachma* and *middos*, of the attribute of kingship.

phrases.he: אך ענין אנא אמלוך שעלה ברצונו ומחשבתו הפשוט,
phrases.en: But the matter of *Ana Emloch* (I shall rule), which arose in His simple will and thought,

phrases.he: היינו כשבא בדבר פרט,
phrases.en: is when it comes into a particular thing,

phrases.he: לבחינת ההשתלשלות בגלוי מהעלמו ההיולי
phrases.en: into *hishtalshelus*, in revelation, out of its *hiyuli* concealment,

phrases.he: כנזכר לעיל במדה דחפץ חסד באדם למטה,
phrases.en: as said above of the attribute of *chafetz chesed* in man below,

phrases.he: וכנזכר לעיל במשל י' כחות הכלולים שבבחינת יחידה,
phrases.en: and as said above in the analogy of the ten powers included in the *yechida*,

phrases.he: בבחינת היולי ועצמיות כו'
phrases.en: as *hiyuli* and essence.

blocks.text: Then *Ana Emloch*, which arose in His simple will and thought. (He stops over the words of the text, "His will and His thought, the simple", and reads them again.) It is when it comes into a particular, into *hishtalshelus*, revealed out of its *hiyuli* concealment. This matter of *Ana Emloch* means that He had a thought to have it in a revelation from the *hiyuli*.

It is as the last chapter said of the attribute of *chafetz chesed* in man below: there, there was the matter of doing the kindness, which means to somebody else. And the same thing is true of the *Malchus*. And as said above in the analogy of the ten powers included in the *yechida*. (He points out a typo in his text: the *yud*, the "ten", is joined to the word *mashal*.)

phrases.he: שאינן נבדלים מן העצם כלל
phrases.en: which are not separate from the essence at all,

phrases.he: וכמו כח התנועה שכלול בעצם החי,
phrases.en: like the power of motion that is included in the essence of the living being,

phrases.he: וכהתפשטות החיות ההיולי הכלול בעצם הנפש ממש כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: and like the spreading forth of the *hiyuli* life included in the very essence of the soul, as said above.

blocks.text: The powers are **not separate from the essence at all**, like the power of motion included in the essence of a living being. And by the way, the *Ana Emloch* is also completely included, even though it is in a particular. That is the matter of *Yachid*, including the *Ana Emloch*.

sections.title: Echad: a spreading forth still inside Himself, unified and simple
sections.summary: *Echad* is the light that spreads forth, but inside the Essence, before the *tzimtzum*: powers seem to separate out and do not. Unity can be spoken of there, unlike in *Yachid*, yet it is still the ten *sefiros* *bli ma* and simple unity.

phrases.he: ולמטה מזה
phrases.en: Below this

phrases.he: הוא בחינת אור אין סוף המאיר ומתפשט
phrases.en: is the *Or Ein Sof* that shines and spreads forth,

phrases.he: והכל עדיין בבחינת עצמותו לפני הצמצום
phrases.en: and all of it is still in His Essence, before the *tzimtzum*;

phrases.he: וזהו הנקרא אחדות הפשוטה
phrases.en: and this is what is called *achdus hapshuta* (simple unity).

blocks.text: **Below this**: now the matter of *Echad*. It is the *Or Ein Sof* that shines and spreads forth, all of it still in His Essence before the *tzimtzum*, and it is called *achdus hapshuta*. In other words, this is still in the *Atzmus Or Ein Sof*. It is not really the spreading forth of the *Or Ein Sof*. It is a spreading forth inside Himself, meaning really the *hiyuli* for the spreading forth.

If you want to give it names, so to speak, you could say that *Echad* is like *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Yachid*, and *Kadmon* is like *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Echad*. Remember what he said in chapter 7: the rule is that the *Malchus* of the lower becomes the *Keser* (crown) of the upper, all the way to the highest of levels. Here, when he says "below this", it means the next level down: the *Malchus* of the upper becomes the *Keser* of the lower.

So the next thing is the level of *Echad*. Over there you can say that at one point these powers came out, so to speak, as if they were separating out; but they are not really separating out. And this can be called *achdus hapshuta*.

phrases.he: שיתכן שם בחינת התכללות ואחדות בעשר ספירות
phrases.en: where one can speak of inclusion and unity in the ten *sefiros*;

phrases.he: וגם הם נקרא עשר ספירות בלי מה,
phrases.en: and they too are called the ten *sefiros* *bli ma* (without what),

phrases.he: כי הוא למעלה גם מבחינת הכנה להשפעה למטה בגלוי עדיין
phrases.en: for it is still above even preparation to give influence below in revelation;

phrases.he: רק שמוכן לצאת מההיולי בדבר פרט
phrases.en: only that it is ready to come out of the *hiyuli* into a particular thing.

blocks.text: There one can speak of division (he reads "division" where the text has "inclusion") and unity in the ten *sefiros*, **and they too are called the ten** *sefiros* *bli ma*: even there it is still *bli ma*; it is not that it is actually ten *sefiros*. Why? Because it is still above even being prepared to give influence below, in revelation.
It is only ready to come out. That means it did not come out of the *hiyuli*; it is still *hiyuli*. You only have to say that at one point it was ready to come out, because it did come out.

phrases.he: כמו חפץ חסד ההיולי הנזכר לעיל,
phrases.en: Like the *hiyuli* *chafetz chesed* mentioned above,

phrases.he: כשבא לענין הרצון וחפץ חסד בהשתלשלות דקו כו'
phrases.en: when it comes to the will and desire for kindness in the *hishtalshelus* of the *Kav*:

phrases.he: גם שלא יצא עדיין בגלוי גמור, גם בעצמו,
phrases.en: even though it has not yet come out in full revelation, even in itself,

phrases.he: על כל פנים שם יתכן בחינת אחדות והתכללות
phrases.en: at any rate there one can speak of unity and inclusion;

phrases.he: רק שנקרא אחדות הפשוטה בהיותו עדיין באור עצמותו הפשוט בתכלית
phrases.en: only it is called simple unity, since it is still in the light of His Essence, utterly simple.

blocks.text: Like the *hiyuli* *chafetz chesed* when it comes to the will for the *hishtalshelus*: **even though it has not yet come out in full revelation, even in itself**. That means He doesn't even know yet what it is, because *Kadmon* here also did not really come out. **at any rate there one can speak of unity and inclusion**: there you could say there is a unification of powers.

blocks.title: When somebody else grabs the bottle
blocks.text: But they are *mamash* totally unified, as even in *Kadmon*. Remember what was said: when somebody else grabs the bottle of vodka, the power of motion changes into the power of speech. Not that it changes from one to the other: up there it is *mamash* the same power.

It is *achdus hapshuta*. In *Yachid* you really can't even call it unity, because there are no powers yet. Here it is called simple unity because it is still in His Essence, **utterly simple**: totally simple.

phrases.he: וכמו בחינת התחלקות שכל ומדות כו' שבחפץ חסד זה,
phrases.en: And like the division into intellect and *middos* in this *chafetz chesed*,

phrases.he: שמחמתו הוא שעלה ברצונו וחכמתו להטיב כו'
phrases.en: because of which it arose in His will and wisdom to do good,

phrases.he: גם טרם בואו לגלוי כלל וכלל כו',
phrases.en: even before it comes into revelation at all,

phrases.he: וכנזכר לעיל במדריגה הב' בנפש האדם.
phrases.en: as said above of the second level in the soul of man.

blocks.text: So too the division into intellect and *middos* in this *chafetz chesed*, because of which it arose in His will and wisdom to do good. It is there **even before it comes into revelation at all**, before it came into an actual revelation, as was explained in chapter 10 of the second level in the soul of man.

sections.title: Kadmon: the whole shiur is ready, and it is made by looking at the mouse
sections.summary: In *Kadmon* the exact *shiur* of the influence, down to the end of *Asiya*, is ready, as the power of motion is ready with the whole movement and still has not moved. But the *shiur* is made by looking at the goal, as the cat looks only at the mouse: that is the *glif glifu*, *Malchus* of *Kadmon*.

phrases.he: והג' כאשר מבחינת חפץ חסד זה הוא שעלה כבר ברצון ושכל כו'
phrases.en: And the third: when from this *chafetz chesed* it has already arisen in will and intellect,

phrases.he: והוכן בכל השיעור באותיות ששיער בעצמו
phrases.en: and is prepared in the whole *shiur* (estimation), in letters, which He estimated in Himself:

phrases.he: איך יהיה איכות אופן ההשפעה ממש לחוץ מעצמותו
phrases.en: how the quality and manner of the influence will be, *mamash*, outside His Essence.

phrases.he: על דרך דוגמא מכח התנועה המוכן איך להניע
phrases.en: By way of example, the power of motion that is ready how to move,

blocks.text: The third level: from this *chafetz chesed* it has already arisen in will and intellect, and is prepared in the whole *shiur*, how the influence will be, *mamash*, outside His Essence. **By way of example, the power of motion that is ready how to move**: in other words, it is already completely ready exactly how to grab the bottle, and it is about to do it.

Somebody once told Rabbi Markel, "We're making up *meshalim* that are not in the book", like the cat and stuff like that; or like right now: where does it say a bottle of vodka in the book? But the *mashal* is straight out of the book. He didn't label it with a bottle of vodka; he didn't give you that example. But he has told you exactly: just as the power of motion is totally ready exactly how it will make the actual motion, all the way to the end of the motion. That is the *mashal*.

The same with the *mashal* of the cat that is going to jump to the top of the wall, or is going to pounce. As a matter of fact, he calls it the power of motion of a living thing, an animal. The cat is going to pounce on a mouse: what, does it say that? It says: the power of motion is ready how to move. It is all, totally, how the manner and quality of the influence will be outside His Essence, till the end of it, to the end of the *Kav*. In various places he mentions *mamash* the end of the *Kav*.

phrases.he: וכח החיות המוכן איך להחיות
phrases.en: and the power of life that is ready how to give life,

phrases.he: כשמוכנים כבר בשיעור ואופן מוגבל,
phrases.en: when they are already prepared in a limited measure and manner,

phrases.he: כנזכר לעיל בענין מדריגה הג' בנפש
phrases.en: as said above of the third level in the soul.

blocks.text: **and the power of life that is ready how to give life**, **when they are already prepared in a limited measure and manner**. In other words: in *Echad* it is just ready to have the powers; in *Kadmon* the actual thing is *mamash* ready, all the way to the end. The motion in the power of motion is *mamash* all ready, but it is still not separate from the power of motion. There is no movement yet.

And not only that: you see that even in *Kadmon* it is still simple unity. When somebody else grabbed the bottle, the power of motion turned into a power of speech; and if somebody else would get the bottle from this guy, then it wouldn't be speech like that either. It is still in *Kadmon*, and it can change from one to the other, **as said above of the third level in the soul**, in chapter 10.

phrases.he: ולמעלה,
phrases.en: And above [in the *nimshal*]:

phrases.he: היינו מה ששיער בעצמות אור אין סוף שנקרא טהירו עילאה
phrases.en: that is, what He estimated in the Essence of the *Or Ein Sof*, called *tehiru ila'a*:

phrases.he: באופן ושיעור מה שרוצה בהשתלשלות
phrases.en: the manner and measure of what He wants in the *hishtalshelus*,

phrases.he: בפועל התגלות דקו עד סוף עולם העשיה
phrases.en: in actual revelation of the *Kav*, to the end of the world of *Asiya*.

phrases.he: שזהו מה שכתוב גליף גליפו בטהירו עילאה
phrases.en: This is what is written, *glif glifu* (He engraved an engraving) in the *tehiru ila'a*,

phrases.he: כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: as said above.

phrases.he: והוא הנקרא בחינת קדמון,
phrases.en: And it is what is called *Kadmon* (preceding):

phrases.he: דהיינו מה שקדם אופן הרצון להשפיע טרם שמשפיע עדיין בגלוי ממש
phrases.en: that is, the manner of the will to give influence that came before, before He actually gives influence in revelation.

phrases.he: וזהו עדיין לפני הצמצום הראשון הנקרא מקום פנוי וחלל כו'
phrases.en: And this is still before the first *tzimtzum*, which is called the *makom panui* (the empty place) and the void,

phrases.he: כנ"ל וד"ל.
phrases.en: as said above; and it is enough for the understanding.

blocks.text: And above, in the *nimshal*: what He estimated in the Essence of the *Or Ein Sof*, the manner and measure of what He wants in the *hishtalshelus*, all the way **to the end of the world of** *Asiya*. *Mamash*: He estimated it in *Kadmon*, which means in the *Atzmus Or Ein Sof*, all the way down to here.

As a matter of fact, the main thing He estimated: in terms of the power of motion, he estimates the whole movement. But the real thing in the power of motion, the whole point of it, is grabbing the bottle, or catching the mouse. That means that even when he is making the *shiur*, he is not thinking about the movement at all. He is thinking about the mouse, or about the bottle of vodka, and the *shiur* comes up automatically according to that. He thinks the bottle, and automatically the whole *shiur* comes up inside him, in the power of motion. That is because it was there the whole time, so it just comes automatically.

blocks.title: The cat does not take out a ruler
blocks.text:
A student: any kind of movement is there in the power of motion; that specific one just comes out. "Right, so that's what I'm saying." But to make the *shiur* he didn't really have to make a *shiur*, the same way you see with the cat. It does not have to sit and think, "Okay, now let me figure out the vector of the jump. Let me think with my algebra class, I gotta get my ruler out and measure the distance between me and the cat" (the mouse, he means). "So wait a minute, now I gotta fix my eyes, so I gotta move my eyes to see where the mouse is."

It is a *shiur* of various powers. Involved in the power of motion is also the power of sight, because you have to see where the bottle is, and there is a triangulation of your eyes to figure out the depth: the two eyes with the bottle make a triangle, so you see where the depth is and how far you have to reach your hand. But you notice that when you do this, you don't think about the *shiur* at all. The *shiur* is secondary.

And it is the same thing with the *tzimtzum*: the real matter of the *tzimtzum* and of the *shiur* is the end of the action. Look at the cat's face. He is moving, the way a cat moves his muscles to get the jump just right, but the whole time his whole focus is on the mouse.

blocks.title: The pitcher
blocks.text: Just like a pitcher in baseball. He is not thinking about how he is going to move his hand; if he did, he would just totally mess up. He is focused on where he wants the ball to go.

blocks.title: Missing the basket
blocks.text: One of them had been reading about it in *Reader's Digest*: a man who teaches, not exactly meditation methods, to basketball players, and also to all kinds of people, for when they make decisions in their lives. When you think too much about how to do it rather than about the goal, that is what screws you up: you'll miss the basket. In other words, if you think of the *shiur* rather than the mouse, you won't get the mouse. You have to forget about the whole thing and just think. In the Eastern martial arts and stuff like that they call it a loss of self. It is not really a loss of self. If you are thinking of how you are going to do it, you lose the spontaneity of the action, and the *shiur* doesn't come out right.

(The next tape picks up the same thought.) The player has to focus not on how he is going to throw it, but just on where it has to end up. So here too, since he is talking about the *shiur* through this example, you understand that the real thing He does is think about the end of it. He does not think about the *shiur* itself.
blocks.outOfPlace: Opens class 006, finishing the analogy with which class 005 ended, before the lines are reread.

blocks.text: The next class reads these lines again. This is what is written, *glif glifu* in the *tehiru ila'a*, and it is called *Kadmon*. Now he is calling the *glif glifu* *Kadmon*. Before, he said that the *glif glifu* is in *Yachid*, and also that it is *Yachid* that is called *tehiru ila'a*. But really that includes *Kadmon*, and the real matter of the *glif glifu* is *davka* (precisely) in *Kadmon*.

*Glif glifu* means that He has a total [will]; later on this is also called the *ratzon hamuchlat* (the absolute will). The *ratzon hamuchlat* is part of the *ratzon hapashut*, not of the composite will. In the simple will there are the simple will and the absolute will; in the composite will there are the general will and the particular will. So the real matter of the *glif glifu* is that it is *Kadmon*.

And the really real matter of the *glif glifu* is *Malchus* of *Kadmon*: the actual letters of the whole thing, when He has made the *shiur* and the whole thing is connected to the thing, the actual final letters of exactly what the definitions of the movement are going to be, till the end of the line. **that is, the manner of the will to give influence that came before**, before it gave influence in actual revelation; and this is still before the first *tzimtzum*, called the *makom panui* and the void. "And that's the recap of chapter 10."

sections.title: The fourth level: the Kav after the tzimtzum, and who really gives the sandwich
sections.summary: What comes after the *tzimtzum*, the *reshimu* and the *Kav* down to *Asiya*, is still called a level of the Essence, though contracted, as the body's motion is to the soul. The physical act does not come from the spiritual will; it comes from the *Aibershter*, which is what *hafshatas hagashmiyus* really means.

phrases.he: ומדריג' הד' הוא מה שאחר הצמצום הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: And the fourth level is what, after the *tzimtzum* mentioned above,

phrases.he: נשאר בחינת הרשימו ונמשך ממנו הקו
phrases.en: the *reshimu* (impression) remained, and from it the *Kav* was drawn,

phrases.he: שהוא בכללות בחינת טהירו תתאה,
phrases.en: which is in general the *tehiru tata'a* (the lower purity),

phrases.he: בחינת מקיף כללי לכל השתלשלות דקו כו'
phrases.en: a general encompassing light for the whole *hishtalshelus* of the *Kav*;

phrases.he: שזהו הבא בבחינת השפעה למטה מן העצמות,
phrases.en: this is what comes as influence below the Essence.

blocks.question: A fourth level? He only told us about three.
blocks.text: Now he is adding. And he says: wait, I did tell you about this fourth level before, that the man of kindness is going to give an actual thing in the actual particular. The *tehiru tata'a*? Not just the *tehiru tata'a*; even after the *tehiru tata'a*. The *tehiru tata'a* is just the *machshava kduma* (the primordial thought). But he said that the whole thing of the man of kindness is that the kindness is what causes the actual giving, the actual act of kindness.

What remains after the *tzimtzum* is the *reshimu*: so the fourth level is the actual world after the *tzimtzum*. And notice that he calls this the fourth level of the *Atzmus Or Ein Sof*. He does not call it another thing. Of what? There is a first level of the *Atzmus Or Ein Sof*, *Yachid*; the second level, *Echad*; the third, *Kadmon*; and then there is a fourth level. And what is the fourth level? What remains after the *tzimtzum*, the *reshimu*, from which the *Kav* is drawn.

The *reshimu* and the *Kav*: by the way, here he is talking about the beginning of the *Kav*, which is the *kav hamida* (the line of measure), the beginning of the *Kav* including the *machshava kduma*. And that is the *tehiru tata'a*, the general encompassing light for the whole *hishtalshelus* of the *Kav*.

**this is what comes as influence below the Essence**. And really it is not just a general encompassing light: it is the whole *hishtalshelus* of the *Kav*, till *Asiya*. Really, that whole thing, to the end, is *mamash* the fourth level of the *Atzmus*, all the way down to here. In other words, it is not a separate thing; it is *mamash* a level of the *Atzmus*.

blocks.question: You just said that it is part of the Atzmus, but he says here that it "comes as influence below the Essence"?
blocks.text: Below the Essence means below the Essence as it is before the *tzimtzum*. The fourth level is a general encompassing light for the whole *hishtalshelus* of the *Kav*, **this is what comes as influence below the Essence**; but there is no real "below the Essence". "Below the Essence" means below the Essence before the *tzimtzum*.
blocks.outOfPlace: Asked after the reading of lines 48-53, about line 47.

phrases.he: כמשל חיות המתפשט בגלוי להחיות כו'
phrases.en: Like the analogy of the life that spreads out in revelation to give life [to the body],

phrases.he: וככח התנועה שמתפשטת להניע הנפעל בגלוי כו'
phrases.en: and the power of motion that spreads out to move the thing moved, in revelation,

phrases.he: שמשתנה ממהות רוחני למהות הגשמה כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: which changes from a spiritual essence to an essence of physicality, as said above;

phrases.he: וכמו צמיחה גשמית מצמיחה רוחנית
phrases.en: or like physical growth from spiritual growth:

phrases.he: כך הוא ערך האור שאחר הצמצום
phrases.en: so is the light after the *tzimtzum*

phrases.he: לגבי האור העצמי שלפני הצמצום
phrases.en: compared to the essential light before the *tzimtzum*.

phrases.he: דמשום זה הוצרך להיות ענין הצמצום הזה,
phrases.en: For this reason this *tzimtzum* had to be,

phrases.he: רק בשביל שיוכל להיות הארת האור שבקו,
phrases.en: only so that there could be the shining of the light in the *Kav*,

phrases.he: שבא בשביל מקור לאבי''ע כידוע
phrases.en: which comes to be a source for *Atzilus*, *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya*, as is known.

blocks.text: He reads the lines through, and then explains them. **Like the analogy of the life that spreads out in revelation to give life**: like how it comes into the body, where it is considered the life of the body, which is like a separate thing. It is like a separate thing; it is not really a separate thing.

blocks.title: An electric current in the arm
blocks.text: **and the power of motion that spreads out to move the thing moved, in revelation**: for instance, the motion that actually moves in your arm is not really your soul. It is electric impulses that move your muscles. As a matter of fact, if you run an electric current through your arm, you can move the muscle without wanting to. It is *mamash* an electric impulse; it is not the soul, really.

**which changes from a spiritual essence to an essence of physicality**, or like physical growth: the actual plant, which comes from spiritual growth, which is just the *hiyuli* in the ground; there is no real growth in the ground. So is the light after the *tzimtzum* compared to the light itself before the *tzimtzum*: it is *mamash* a contracted thing.

It is like a motion compared to the actual brain, or like the act compared to the power of motion itself. Or like an idea compared to the actual power of the intellect, because the power of the intellect is not an idea at all. And this *tzimtzum* had to be only so that there could be the shining of the light in the *Kav*, as a source for *Atzilus*, *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya*.

phrases.he: אך עם כל זה
phrases.en: But nonetheless,

phrases.he: הרי כל פרטי העשר ספירות דאבי''ע,
phrases.en: all the particulars of the ten *sefiros* of *Atzilus*, *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya*,

phrases.he: הכל כלולים מתחלה בעצמות אור אין סוף
phrases.en: all of it is included from the start in the Essence of the *Or Ein Sof*,

phrases.he: בבחינת היולי ועצמי
phrases.en: as *hiyuli* and essence;

phrases.he: ואחר כך על ידי הצמצום
phrases.en: and afterwards, through the *tzimtzum*,

phrases.he: משתנה לפי אופן מוגבל
phrases.en: it changes into a limited manner

phrases.he: בהשפעה הכללית דקו בבחינת סובב
phrases.en: in the general influence of the *Kav*, as *sovev* (encompassing).

blocks.text: **But nonetheless**, all the particulars of the ten *sefiros* of *Atzilus*, *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya*, all the particulars all the way to the end of *Asiya*, are all included first in the Essence of the *Or Ein Sof*, "because otherwise where did they come from?" They are there as *hiyuli* and essence. And afterwards, through the *tzimtzum*, it changes into a limited manner, in the general influence of the *Kav*.

So now we get back to what was spoken of before, *hafshatas hagashmiyus* (stripping away the physical). What is the physical? The physical is a *tzimtzum*. That means the physical is less than the actual thing. And it is not the same thing as spiritual to physical, because the spiritual does not actually cause the physical.

blocks.title: Who really gives the sandwich
blocks.text: Spiritual to physical is like when we say that the kindness of a person, in his soul, which is spiritual, causes him to give the sandwich. But that is not true. It is not like in the *nimshal*: in the *mashal* the kindness only causes him to have the will to give the sandwich. The actual giving of the sandwich is done by the *Aibershter* Himself, who moves his body and gives him the money. Because if the *Aibershter* hadn't given him the money, he would be the poor man. He didn't make himself the rich man. So the spiritual is a separate matter: the spiritual does not cause the physical.

blocks.title: I ain't got that kind of money
blocks.text: And not only that: he doesn't even know how to move his arm, or to send the electric impulses to give the sandwich, or even to make a sandwich. He didn't make the sandwich at all. And even the money he bought the sandwich with, really the *Aibershter* gave him. He just wanted to give the sandwich. Somebody else says, "I'd like to help a lot of people, but I ain't got that kind of money," even though his will for kindness could be just as strong as the other guy's, maybe even stronger.

So the real *hafshatas hagashmiyus* is, in a way, the opposite of what they think. They say, "Oh, you should forget about the physical and think about the spiritual." But really the physical does not come from the spiritual. The actual physical act of doing the kindness does not come from the real spiritual kindness of the man's soul. Only the will to do the kindness is there, and according to the will, as it says, "in the way a man wants to go, he is led." In other words, you only make the decision of the will; then the *Aibershter* moves your body for you.

And that is the whole terrible thing of a sin, and the whole wonderful thing of a mitzva. When you decide to do it, the *Aibershter* has to actually go and help you do this bad thing. It is like somebody who takes the king's head and puts it in the toilet: it says it in the *Tanya* like that. You are forcing the *Aibershter* to help you out with this thing. And when you decide in the morning to put on tefillin, you are letting the *Aibershter* have a *dira b'tachtonim* (a dwelling below). He gets to put on tefillin, which is what He wanted to do.

But the thing is that the physical action really did not come from you. And *hafshatas hagashmiyus* means that by the *Aibershter* it is not like that; it is not like it is with your physicality. You think the *mashal* is like the *nimshal*, but the *mashal* is physical. The sandwich did not come from the kindness. Only the desire to do a kindness and to give a sandwich came from the kindness of the soul, the spiritual kindness. But if you strip away the physical, by the *Aibershter* it is not like that: the actual sandwich came from Him.

So the whole matter of *hafshatas hagashmiyus*: they have it backwards. It is the same as when you say that there is no *chachma* up above: somebody who has it backwards doesn't understand. It doesn't mean there is no *chachma*; there is a whole bunch of *chachma* up there. "The *Aibershter* is super, super, super smart." It is just that it is in a way that is a total *hiyuli*, so you can't even call it *chachma*. That is the *hiyuli* in Himself; and afterwards, through the *tzimtzum*, it comes down into the general influence of the *Kav*.

phrases.he: והרי זה כדוגמת חיות הנפש הרוחנית כשבאה להחיות הגוף
phrases.en: This is like the life of the spiritual soul when it comes to give life to the body,

phrases.he: שכלולה ברוחניות מכל פרטי חיות הגשמיות, ראיה ושמיעה שבגוף הגשמי כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: which includes, spiritually, all the particulars of physical life, sight and hearing in the physical body, as said above.

phrases.he: (וענין הצמצום והרשימה יתבאר בסמוך)
phrases.en: (And the matter of the *tzimtzum* and the *reshimu* will be explained shortly.)

blocks.text: **This is like the life of the spiritual soul when it comes to give life to the body**, which includes, spiritually, all the particulars of physical life, sight and hearing, as explained in chapter 10. ("And I'm going to have to stop over here." "All right." "Go ahead.") The matter of the *tzimtzum* and the *reshimu* will be explained shortly.

sections.title: "Blessed is He who spoke": the levels in the words of the prayer
sections.summary: The words of *Baruch She'amar* name the levels: "spoke" is the hidden will in *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof*, "and the world came to be" is the *shiur* of *Kadmon* and the *Kav*, "says and does" is what is drawn into the *Kav*, down to *Adam Kadmon* and the *kav hamida*. The point is to tie chapters 10 and 11 to the intentions of prayer.

phrases.he: (וזהו פירוש כללי למה שכתוב ברוך שאמר והיה העולם
phrases.en: (And this is a general explanation of what is said, "Blessed is He who spoke, and the world came to be":

phrases.he: פירוש שאמר בהעלם,
phrases.en: "spoke" means in concealment,

phrases.he: ברצונו הפשוט שבמלכות דאין סוף,
phrases.en: in His simple will in *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof*,

phrases.he: בהיותו עדיין כלול בחפץ חסד העצמי הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: while it is still included in the essential *chafetz chesed* mentioned above;

phrases.he: ואחר כך והיה,
phrases.en: and afterwards, "came to be":

phrases.he: בגלוי אור המתפשט לדבר פרט להשתלשלות,
phrases.en: in revelation, the light that spreads forth into a particular thing, into *hishtalshelus*,

phrases.he: להיות מקור לכל העולמות
phrases.en: to be a source for all the worlds.

phrases.he: ופירוש והיה העולם,
phrases.en: And "the world came to be" means

phrases.he: היינו דווקא מן מה ששיער בעצמו בכח
phrases.en: *davka* from what He estimated in Himself, in potential,

phrases.he: שהוא שרש מה שמתהווה אחר כך העולם הכללי שנמשך מן הקו
phrases.en: which is the root of what afterwards comes to be, the general world, drawn from the *Kav*,

phrases.he: וכו' וכנזכר לעיל ודי למבין.
phrases.en: as said above; and it is enough for the understanding.

blocks.text: This is a general explanation of what we say, "Blessed is He who spoke, and the world came to be." "Spoke" is in concealment, in the simple will in *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof*, while it is all still in the essential *chafetz chesed*. Then "came to be": in revelation, the light spreading forth into a particular, into *hishtalshelus*, to be a source for all the worlds. And "the world came to be" is *davka* from what He estimated in Himself in potential, the root from which the general world drawn from the *Kav* comes to be afterwards. That means the general worlds: as was said, *Adam Kadmon* is the Adam of *Beriya*.

phrases.he: וברוך הוא, נסתר,
phrases.en: And "Blessed is He": "He" is hidden;

phrases.he: היינו בחינת קדמונו של עולם
phrases.en: that is, the *Kadmon* of the world,

phrases.he: דהיינו מה ששיער בעצמו בכח כו'
phrases.en: that is, what He estimated in Himself, in potential.

phrases.he: וכמו שכתוב מגיד מראשית אחרית,
phrases.en: As it is written, "He tells the end from the beginning":

phrases.he: מראשית הקו עד סופו כו'
phrases.en: from the beginning of the *Kav* to its end.

phrases.he: ומקדם אשר לא נעשה עדיין
phrases.en: "And from before, what was not yet done":

phrases.he: היינו מקדמונו של עולם הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: that is, from the *Kadmon* of the world mentioned above,

phrases.he: ונקרא ימי קדם,
phrases.en: and it is called *yemei kedem* (the days of old),

phrases.he: שקודם למה שנמשך בקו
phrases.en: which precede what is drawn into the *Kav*;

phrases.he: והוא מה שקדם בעצמו בכח, מה שעתיד להיות בפועל כו' ודי למבין.
phrases.en: and it is what preceded in Himself, in potential, what would later be in actuality; and it is enough for the understanding.

blocks.text: "And blessed is He": "He" means hidden, the *Kadmon* of the world, what He estimated in Himself in potential. As it says, "He tells the end from the beginning": **from the beginning of the** *Kav* till the end of the *Kav*.

"And from before, what was not yet done": "before" means that even before the *tzimtzum* He tells what wasn't even made yet. Even before it was made, He already told you; He already knew what it is going to be. It is called *yemei kedem*, which precede what is drawn into the *Kav*. In other places he will sometimes say that *yemei kedem* is a different thing, but here *yemei kedem* means the *middos* in *Kadmon*, before they even came into the *Kav*. **and it is what preceded in Himself, in potential, what would later be in actuality**: the *glif glifu* in *Kadmon*, where the *shiur* is.

phrases.he: ומה שכתוב ברוך אומר ועושה כו',
phrases.en: And what is said, "Blessed is He who says and does":

phrases.he: היינו מה שנמשך בקו בפועל ממש
phrases.en: that is what is drawn into the *Kav* in actual fact.

phrases.he: ועושה בראשית כו',
phrases.en: "Who does the work of creation":

phrases.he: הוא כל שיעור קומת אדם קדמון כו'
phrases.en: it is the whole *shiur koma* (full stature) of *Adam Kadmon*.

blocks.text: "Blessed is He who says and does": that is what is drawn into the *Kav* in actual fact. He says, and He did it. "Who does the work of creation" is the whole *shiur koma* of *Adam Kadmon*, which is the Adam of *Beriya*.

This whole business seems as though it really should be about *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya*. But he is talking about it as far as the *Aibershter* is concerned, and as far as the *Aibershter* is concerned, *Atzilus* is the end of *Asiya*. So what it says, it says as from the *Aibershter*: "who does the work of creation." Really, by us, *Atzilus* is the work of the chariot, and the work of creation is how *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya* come out of *Malchus* of *Atzilus*. But as far as the *Aibershter* is concerned, *Asiya* is already in *Adam Kadmon*.

phrases.he: וגוזר ומקיים, בתחלה,
phrases.en: "Decrees and fulfils": first,

phrases.he: הוא בחינת קו המדה שלפני אדם קדמון
phrases.en: it is the *kav hamida* (the line of measure) before *Adam Kadmon*,

phrases.he: שהוא בחינת צמצום דרשימו שנמשך ממנו הקו כידוע,
phrases.en: which is the *tzimtzum* of the *reshimu* from which the *Kav* is drawn, as is known,

phrases.he: וכמו שיתבאר בעזרת השם בסמוך):
phrases.en: and as will be explained shortly, with G-d's help.)

blocks.text: "Decrees and fulfils": first, it is the *kav hamida* before *Adam Kadmon*; that is the decree. It is the *tzimtzum* of the *reshimu* from which the *Kav* is drawn, as will be explained shortly. And this whole teaching was basically to connect chapters 10 and 11 to the *kavanos* (intentions) in *davenen* (prayer).

reviewQuestions.question: Why is the whole *hishtalshelus* to Him only a *prat*, like fidgeting with your ear, and why is the study of *Chassidus* the exception?
Why does one say *makor l'makor* rather than simply that He is the source?
In which of *Yachid*, *Echad* and *Kadmon* can one speak of unity, and why is it still called simple unity?
What does the cat pouncing on the mouse show about how the *shiur* of *Kadmon* is made?
Why is what comes after the *tzimtzum* called the fourth level of the Essence, and what does "below the Essence" mean?
In what way do people have *hafshatas hagashmiyus* backwards, and what does the sandwich show?

notes.text: Class 005 reads line 1 with "בעצם" for "בנפש" and line 40 with "יחיד לעילא" for "טהירו עילאה"; class 006 rereads lines 40-41 in a different wording ("מה שנתבאר בעצמותו שאינו נתפס... שיעור ממש הרשום בהשתלשלות"). The transcript may be mishearing; the phrases follow the chapter text.

The discussion of the Rebbe Rashab (005 w142-1014) has no speaker labels and student and teacher alternate quickly; the blocks give the content without always saying who said which sentence. "A maamar of the Rebbe, either in yud-daled or yud-zayin" is left as he said it: it is not clear whether he means years (5714, 5717) or volumes.
"These 78 pages" is presumably Shaar HaYichud as printed in his edition.

The pitcher and the Reader's Digest story (005 w3829-4103) pass between two speakers with no labels. The voice that says it read the Reader's Digest piece (w3885-3955) runs on without a break into w4007-4103, which is in Rabbi Markel's own vocabulary ("if you think of the shiur rather than the mouse", "not really a loss of self"), so it is probably he who read it; the story block keeps the hedge "one of them". A listener should decide.
The phone-and-brother joke (005 w1407-1416) is its own aside, flagged private; it also suggests the class is held over the phone with his brother.
In line 23 he points out a typo in his printed text ("the yud is connected to the mashal"); he does not say what it should read. Not checked against the chapter file, which reads "במשל י' כחות".
He reads line 29 with "התחלקות" (division) for "התכללות" (inclusion); the block follows his reading, the phrase follows the text.
The vodka analogy (somebody else grabs the bottle, the power of motion becomes a power of speech) is from the class on chapter 10; here it is only referred to.
Class 006 has Sofer times, not re-timed ones; the seconds of its blocks may be off.
"Adam Kadmon is Adam of Beriya" (006 w2001-2014, w2175-2185) is reported as he said it, "like you said", referring to an earlier remark of the student.
"The king's head in the toilet" is his citation of the Tanya's image for a sin; kept as said, not flagged, since it is the Tanya's own.
Lines 48-53 are read straight through (006 w726-780) and then explained after a question about line 47 (w781-853); the question is placed under line 47 with outOfPlace.
